doc.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022

title: Would he write an 'Is Jazz Dead?' article
summary: He is reluctant to take on the perennial question, calling jazz an evolving Black-American art form and pointing to thriving schools.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Wow that’s fascinating. Have you ever had someone propose that you write an article with a title something like “Is Jazz Dead?” You know every ten years, maybe less than that, it seems like this shows up on the cover of DownBeat or Jazz Times.
And it’s something to write about. Would you take that on?

I don’t know. I would be 51 percent no, 49 percent maybe. And I’ll tell you why. There has been a lot written about that, a lot discussed about that, it is a philosophical question. It’s a question that plays directly into jazz education. It’s a question that plays into access to technology. It is a very, very, very deep question that quite frankly I would say I don’t care to debate it, all I know is that it is a perennial art form that is a Black-American and American art form that is still evolving. Not only is it evolving but it’s like a mobius. It goes back — you know Marsalis is marvelous about doing this, you know going back to its roots, going back to its roots, and then moving ahead and examining different pathways that jazz artists have taken. You know John Coltrane being one of the most avid explorers, Thelonious Monk and many, many, many others. So you know I wouldn’t go back and comment well it smells that way, like you hear people say, which is stupid. But it’s the kind of thing that let’s just say I would have to take a long, long, long walk thinking about if I would want to do it, what are some of the factors both positive and negative. You know it’s really interesting in the sense like I say, this plays to jazz education. If jazz is dead why are there so many great high school and college jazz ensembles? Okay?
